# rm safety hook — design intent (packs/general/deletions.py)

Shipped in 9.19.0 (commit 8e32bb48, 2026-07-16) after two adversarial codex review passes (finder: 8 findings, refuter: 10; 9 fixes accepted, 3 classes deliberately rejected). Restructured in the 2026-07-17 styleguide wave: `GLOB_LIMIT` is the module's only surviving constant (user directive: constants inline unless divergence-would-be-a-bug or cross-module-shared); the per-`rm` handling lives in the `handle_rm` helper.

## Threat model

This is an **accident guard, not a security boundary**. It lexically analyzes the pre-execution Bash command; a determined evader always wins (see the removed read-only approver, cc-notes/memory: static lexical proof is unsound). The asymmetry that makes this sound where the approver wasn't: a **blocker fails safe** — a missed spelling is just the pre-hook status quo, while a false block costs one agent roundtrip and the deny message says what to do instead.

## Rules and thresholds

- **(a) Outside-repo block**: any literal target (or any glob *match*) whose path has no `.git`/`.jj` marker in itself or an ancestor. `.git` may be a FILE (worktrees/submodules) — the check is `.exists()`, never `.is_dir()`. Exemption: `captain_hook/util/scratch.is_scratch_path` (TEMP_ROOTS incl. `/run/user/<uid>`, scratch-named ancestor dirs). That predicate is the **shared seam** with `packs/fixes/scratch_writes.py` and the future cc-transcript session-scratchpad locator (its paths resolve under TEMP_ROOTS already) — never fork a second scratch definition.
- **(b) Glob limit**: `GLOB_LIMIT = 10` (user-picked 2026-07-15). Counting is bounded (islice / budgeted walk) — never a full expansion. **Deliberately NOT scratch-exempt**: an 11-file glob blocks even in /tmp.
- **(c) Repo-root block**: a literal target that is itself a repo root (marker directly inside) — deleting it destroys the history that makes rule (a)'s recoverability argument work. Glob matches get the same check; glob *prefixes* don't (bash `*` skips dotfiles, so `.git` survives `rm repo/*`).
- **Walk budget**: `**` patterns walk at most 20,000 entries (inlined literal in `recursive_glob_matches`; os.walk with `followlinks=False` — symlink loops confirmed miscounting under iglob). Budget exhaustion **fails closed** ("too broad to verify safely"). The boundary is tested by monkeypatching the `walked_paths` filesystem seam with synthetic paths — never by patching a constant (none exists). Non-`**` globs stay on `glob.iglob` (naturally bounded).

## Symlink policy

The leaf is **never dereferenced**: `rm` unlinks the directory entry, not the referent, so `resolve_target` resolves the parent and preserves the final component. Confirmed both failure directions pre-fix: an outside symlink into the repo was allowed (bypass), an in-repo symlink pointing outside was denied (FP).

## cwd and token semantics

- Linear `cd` tracking walks the command line updating the effective cwd; an unresolvable `cd` (`$VAR`, `-`, no arg) sets it to None and subsequent **relative** targets skip (fail-open — cd-tracking failure must not poison later commands).
- `$`-containing **rm targets** evaluate as literal paths (fail-closed; pinned by test `test_normalizes_executable_and_path_token`). This asymmetry with cd is deliberate.
- Tokens and executables get shell dequoting + backslash unescaping + casefolded basename (`\rm`, `'rm'`, `/BIN/RM` on APFS all normalize to rm) — local normalization that duplicates what cc-transcript should own; delete it when backlog task d026e9cd lands upstream and the pin bumps.

## Deliberate punts — do not "fix" locally

- **Wrapper option arity** (`env -u HOME rm`, `sudo -u root rm`, `timeout 5s rm` pass through): `Command.unwrapped` limitation, upstream task d026e9cd. A local heuristic (e.g. "rm anywhere in args") false-positives on `echo rm foo`.
- **Brace expansion** (`rm {safe,..}/x`): bypass needs mixed in/out branches — adversarial-shaped, not accident-shaped.
- **Quoted globs / quoted tilde** (`rm '*.py'`, `rm '~/f'`): parser dequotes before the hook sees tokens; accepted FPs.
- **`xargs rm` stdin targets, `find -delete`/`-exec rm`, `$(...)`** (dropped by parser entirely): out of scope.

## Testing landmines

- pytest `tmp_path` is **scratch-exempt through TWO independent branches**, and both must be neutralized in every rule-(a)/repo-root block test: on macOS it sits under `/var/folders` (a TEMP_ROOT); on Linux it sits under `/tmp/...`, so `"tmp"` appears in `resolved.parts[:-1]` and the `SCRATCH_DIR_NAMES` name-ancestor branch matches **even with TEMP_ROOTS patched empty**. This shipped green-but-wrong once: 8e32bb48 passed every macOS run and failed 4 tests on Linux CI. Use the shared `no_scratch` fixture in `tests/test_pack_deletions.py` (patches both globals); reproduce the Linux topology locally with `TMPDIR=/tmp uv run pytest tests/test_pack_deletions.py`.
- Inline tests run on the real filesystem — only machine-independent cases belong there (`cwd="/"` absolute-path cases); fixture-dependent cases live in `tests/test_pack_deletions.py`.
- Shell `echo` mangles `\r` in hand-rolled JSON probes — use `printf`/files when live-testing escaped spellings through `.venv/bin/hook run PreToolUse`.
